label: first token is m (t=0)
explanation: Binary feature that fires only at step 0 when the first original token is m, with a constant magnitude of about 1.544 on every one of these steps. It does not fire on m at any later position, on any other first token, or in the delimiter or copy phases. Sequence length, digit count, and repeats of the token have no effect on magnitude. The only exception in dev is one very weak (0.07x) activation at the copy step that re-inputs m as the first output.

issues: I found no systematic counterexample. On the test split, misses reported 0 missed activations and 0 false positives, and precision, recall, F1 and correlation were all 1.0.

The profile confirms the claims. On dev the feature is active on 16624 steps, and 16623 of them are at t=0 (100% of activation mass). Mean, median and max magnitude are all 1.544. It never fires in the delimiter phase, and only once in the copy phase (t=10, recall_idx=1).

Scoring (t >= L) & (in_tok == m) on dev gave F1 ~2e-5, which supports the claim that the feature does not fire when m is re-input during the copy phase. The one copy-phase activation is a single noise event.
